Today, many nuns wear this distinctive attire, yet on her inaugural day in the slums, Mother Teresa was entirely solitary—just a single woman, devoid of assistance or financial resources. How did she embark on her mission? She began by praying fervently to God, then ventured into the slum. There, she engaged with impoverished children, many of whom were homeless, orphaned, and deprived of education. She initiated informal lessons right on the street. The children responded warmly, and by the following day, a considerable number gathered at her makeshift ‘school,’ returning daily thereafter. 

One day, she encountered a frail, elderly woman lying in the street—homeless, gravely ill, and rejected by hospital doctors due to her poverty and age. This woman was on the brink of death, utterly alone without family or support. Passersby avoided her, yet Mother Teresa approached, spoke to her gently, bathed her, and remained by her side. Though the woman eventually passed away, she did so not in solitude but clasping the hand of a compassionate friend. Such scenes of suffering and imminent death were all too common in those streets.<|eot_id|>
